options.text: The mark stands for a point: a precise location with no length, breadth, or thickness, named by the letter $A$.
The ink blob itself is the geometric object, so its visible size on the paper is the point.
Any decorative smudge is a point, even when it does not name a location.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

stem: Alok makes a tiny ink pin-prick on plain paper and labels it $A$.

part_answers.answer: A point is an exact location with no size; the ink mark is only a model, and the capital letter A names that location.

teacher.key_rationale: The pin-prick models a sizeless location named A. Treating the ink size as the point omits the no-size condition. Calling any smudge a point stretches the idea beyond named locations.
